A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.", "room": "The phrase 'A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way': either it means such a verse counts only under the just-stated conditions (the judge must quote the earlier-round sentence that pressed it against the link and name that round), or it means such a verse counts toward breaking a link without those conditions; I weighed the first reading because 'this way' points back to the conditions just stated, and the second reading would leave the sentence with nothing to do.", "why": "The judge broke C3's link with Matthew 1:18, 25 (and Luke 1:34) while quoting only scripture, never the sentence of an earlier round that pressed these verses against that link, and naming no round (the rounds-named line is empty), so under K-G4 these verses do not count and the link-break stands on verses the rule disqualifies."}
